Use case: ads-marketing. Create one finished flat opaque landscape 16:9 Korean neighborhood repair workshop poster for social media and local community display.

Whole visual design: an asymmetric editorial story composed of unequal, unframed brush-and-ink episodes across the width. The visual story is substantial and content-specific: the same blue-black wooden chair with a red-orange seat has a loose leg joint in the opening, is steadied and tightened by two neighbors in the larger shared-work episode, and stands soundly in the result episode. The same pale lavender shirt has a distinct small tear at its lower front, receives a red-orange fabric patch with visible stitch logic during a neighbor's repair gesture, and is shown usable with that stitched patch. These are several intimate scenes at different scales, not numbered instructions or a uniform comic grid. Neighbor gestures show cooperation: one hand steadies the chair frame while another neighbor turns a screwdriver at the loose joint; another pair of people holds the cloth flat while a needle and thread attach its patch. Make hand ownership, grip, chair rails and contact points legible with economical confident drawing. The story should convey sharing tools and learning together without additional written captions.

Resolve the body area as part of this story before sizing the title. At a 720px-wide viewing assumption, give the continuous explanation paragraph a substantial 15–17px optical body, a broad lower-center reading area, comfortable line spacing and strong blue-black contrast. Let the opening chair silhouette occupy the left side down into the lower half; the larger cooperation episode spreads through the upper middle; a smaller repaired-result episode occupies the upper right. The different silhouettes and their reaching arms create an irregular broad rhythm and open a generous continuous text space at lower center, rather than a horizontal picture strip above an information template. The headline enters the open space among the repaired-result scene near the right of center, in two sturdy balanced Korean word groups. It is expressive but leaves the explanation fully spacious. Place the short English line close to the headline, and the promise line at the start of the lower-center explanation area. The long explanation is one continuous left-aligned paragraph, soft-wrapped at meaningful word boundaries into roughly three lines, never broken across the episodes. Its left edge and the adjacent opening drawing guide the eye into the information immediately below.

Immediately beneath and adjacent to the explanation, use two functionally connected groups with common line starts and generous distinction in spacing: the workshop name followed by date, time, venue and fee in one group, and deadline, bring-an-item invitation and URL in the neighboring group. They are large enough to read comfortably at the 720px assumption; no tiny footer copy. The date and time can share a line while remaining separate exact strings. Keep invitation as a natural continuous line or soft wrapping. Make the information part of this irregular image-led composition; no border boxes, equal cards or evenly labeled corners. No decorative lines are necessary to explain the route.

Visual grammar and finish: deliberate saturated red-orange, blue-black ink and pale lavender painted areas on a light paper-colored ground. Large irregular painted shapes belong to the clothing, chair and human silhouettes. Vary image line weight intentionally: thick expressive contours and a few precise thin joint, patch and thread lines. Controlled dry-brush edges in illustration only, clean silhouettes, no generic splatter or arbitrary ornament. Warm, capable neighbors of different adult ages, recognizable workshop actions without detailed room dressing. Precise front-plane print for every text entry. The body and information use mature Korean serif forms with restrained stroke contrast, open and consistent counters, sturdy stems, uniform baselines and clearly separated words; Latin, figures and punctuation have balanced optical size. Title can have sturdy hand-ink character only with fully mature exact Hangul proportions. Do not impose drawing texture, slanted perspective or wobbly baselines on the small text.

Print exactly these entries, each once, preserving Korean, capitalization, numeric forms, meaningful word spaces and punctuation. Layout wrapping may change, but no content is added, repeated or omitted:
